newsitem.title: USA: Ford cuts $1 billion in costs in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Ford cuts $1 billion in costs in Q2.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday it slashed total automotive costs by $1 billion in the second quarter, bringing its first-half cost-cutting total to $1.8 billion.
The automaker said it does not expect to achieve another $1.8 billion in cost savings for the second half of 1997, but it expects to have total cost reductions for the year of more than $2 billion.
Ford originally targeted cost savings of $1 billion for all of 1997. The U.S. No. 2 automaker today reported record second quarter profits of $2.53 billion, or $2.06 a share.

Ford officials said the cost savings are calculated assuming constant volume and mix. Cost improvements were made in several areas, including lower material costs through design immprovements and supplier efficiencies; quality-related costs such as warranty and production efficiencies; manufacturing process improvements; engineering and investment efficiencies, and lower launch costs.
For the first half of 1997, Ford said its capital spending was $3.5 billion, a decrease of $83 million from a year ago.
Ford has a target of holding its 1997 full-year capital spending to the same level as 1996, which was $8.2 billion.
